info.title: Comprehensive Basic English Grammar Test
info.description: Tests basic English grammar including verb agreement, tenses, prepositions, pronouns, and sentence structure.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: She ___ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subject 'She' requires the verb form 'goes' in the present simple tense.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: They ___ playing football right now.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'They' requires the plural verb 'are' in the present continuous tense.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: I ___ a movie last night.
questions.explanation: The time marker 'last night' indicates the past simple tense, so the regular verb 'watched' is correct.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: We ___ visit Paris next year.
questions.explanation: The future time marker 'next year' requires the future simple auxiliary verb 'will'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: The book is ___ the table.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'on' is used to indicate a surface, which fits the context of a book resting on a table.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: He is ___ honest man.
questions.explanation: The word 'honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so the article 'an' is required.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: This is my book. It belongs to ___.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'to' requires an object pronoun, which is 'me'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: This car is ___ than that one.
questions.explanation: When comparing two things, the comparative form 'faster' is used, followed by 'than'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: She is the ___ student in the class.
questions.explanation: When comparing one person to a group, the superlative form 'smartest' is used.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: How ___ water do you drink daily?
questions.explanation: 'Water' is an uncountable noun, so it requires the quantifier 'much'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: There are ___ apples in the basket.
questions.explanation: 'Some' is used in positive sentences with plural countable nouns like 'apples'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: You ___ wear a seatbelt while driving.
questions.explanation: 'Must' is used to express a strong obligation or rule, which applies to wearing a seatbelt.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: I wanted to go, ___ I was too tired.
questions.explanation: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to show contrast between two clauses.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: I have ___ my homework already.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense ('have' + past participle) requires the past participle 'finished'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: Is this ___ pen?
questions.explanation: A possessive adjective ('your') is needed before the noun 'pen' to show ownership.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: He runs very ___.
questions.explanation: An adverb ('quickly') is required to modify the verb 'runs'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: ___ is your birthday?
questions.explanation: 'When' is the correct interrogative word to ask about a date or time.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: ___ a lot of people at the party.
questions.explanation: 'There are' is used because 'people' is a plural countable noun.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: ___ the door, please.
questions.explanation: Imperative sentences (commands or requests) use the base form of the verb, 'Close'.

questions.description: Select the best answer from A-D. Read all options carefully.
questions.question: I enjoy ___ books.
questions.explanation: The verb 'enjoy' is always followed by a gerund (verb + -ing), so 'reading' is correct.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: He go to the store yesterday.
questions.explanation: The time marker 'yesterday' requires the past simple tense, so 'go' must be corrected to 'went'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: They is happy to see us.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'They' requires the plural verb 'are', not the singular 'is'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.explanation: The plural form of 'child' is irregular and must be 'children'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.explanation: Modal verbs like 'can' are always followed by the base form of the verb, without 's'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: We was waiting for the bus.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'We' requires the plural past tense verb 'were', not 'was'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., doesn't / does not).
questions.explanation: Third-person singular subjects require 'doesn't' or 'does not' in the present simple negative.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: This is the more beautiful flower.
questions.explanation: When comparing one item to a whole group, the superlative 'most' is required, not the comparative 'more'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: I have saw that movie before.
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense requires the past participle 'seen', not the past simple 'saw'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: She is married with a doctor.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition to use with 'married' is 'to', not 'with'.

questions.description: Click the incorrect word in the sentence, then type the correction. Multiple forms accepted (e.g., contractions or full words).
questions.sentence: He is taller then his brother.
questions.explanation: 'Than' is used for comparisons, while 'then' is used for time sequences.
